title: Baptiste de Lille's story
summary: Trombonist who spent years in Jacksonville and came back to play again; the talk drifts to wives who stayed away.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Can you tell me about, some more about Baptiste de Lille? I never got to know him. He died long before my time. I wonder. No, I don't think so.
I didn't live here you see until a few years ago, so I never knew him.
But this is what happened to him. He uh, went out of the audible mile. Oh I believe I heard that. And he stayed in Jacksonville about 14 or 15 years.
That ball? I didn't know. And then when he came back, you know he pinned up on the trombone. Just like that. And played again?
Yeah. Was he really very good? Good.
Was he good? He was a good trombone player. Very good musician. Fine man, band man.
Do you know about when he died? How long he's been gone?
No, not too long, but less than 10 years about that.

I didn't know. I didn't know. Very good. Now, he stayed in Jackson 14 years, but his wife wouldn't send him to get him. And I don't know how he got here, but when he got here, he wasn't alone, she died. Well I know two men that happened there.

I know another oldwood parish like that. A man's wife was in Jackson and she was writing the little son to get him. And the church sent him and got him. And when she come home, he's gone about 15, 16 years. And when she come, he died about a year. So after that. That's great. He wouldn't send him to get her.
Did Leo play slide all the time or at one time? Very good.
I didn't know him when he played the guy, but I think he did. You only heard him on the slide then? Yeah, that was at Lincoln Park then. Yeah, that was at Lincoln Park then.
